outcome: Contraception utilization patterns (types of methods used, effectiveness)
cohort: A total of 307 volunteering female refugees and asylum seekers aged 18-63 (mean 33 years) from community shelters in Berlin, predominantly from Syria and Afghanistan, participated in the study.
finding: Despite the provision of free family planning services, 47% of women requiring contraception had an unmet need, and many others relied on less effective traditional birth control methods.
